request.goal: Reduce full graph encoder inference latency for the standard workload, preserving the full output checks.
notes: Command provenance: user command 'python infer.py --workload standard --output /tmp/original-graph' (inputs/intent.json); README.md:10 shows the same entry with a different --output directory.

Objective metric key latency_ms is the sample field recorded in infer.py:59; it is wall-clock time of one synchronized full-graph forward (full request), not cached-only throughput. Source goal declared at workloads.json:13.

Quality compares the complete output tensor with torch.testing.assert_close(actual, reference, atol=1e-05, rtol=1e-4) (infer.py:45, tolerances from workloads.json:9); output shape [4096, 64] float32. No discrete outputs require exact comparison.

Numerical policies to preserve (infer.py:13-17): torch.manual_seed(20261021) for weights, separate CPU generator seeded seed+1 for the input fixture, allow_tf32=False for matmul and cudnn, float32_matmul_precision('highest'), dtype float32 (workloads.json:11).

Architecture (model.py:18-26): two-layer mean GraphSAGE, Linear(2*in->out) per layer, input_features=128, hidden_features=256, output_features=64 (workloads.json:2), ReLU between layers. Duplicate directed edges contribute individually to mean aggregation; nodes without incoming edges use zero neighbor features (README.md:17-19, model.py:12-14).
Inference has no cross-invocation state (README.md:19); each adapter.run() is an independent forward with the same GPU-resident inputs.
Model and input construction, quality checking, statistics and report writing are outside timing (README.md:13-15).

workloads.json:14-15 also declares a secondary memory goal (peak_allocated_bytes, minimize, with constraint graphs_per_second ge baseline_ratio 0.95); the user goal selects the latency goal, so it is recorded here, not added to the objective constraints.
held_out_workloads entry unseen_graph (7168 nodes, 143360 edges, workloads.json:7) is not selected.
Single-process CUDA workload: prepare() targets device 'cuda' (infer.py:12) and there is no distributed initialization; device_count=1 from the deployment inventory.

One measured invocation: One complete graph encoder forward on GPU-resident inputs: infer(model, inputs) (infer.py:29-30) running GraphEncoder.forward(features, sources, destinations, degree) under torch.inference_mode() for the standard workload row, returning the full [4096, 64] FP32 output tensor. Model/fixture construction and H2D transfer (infer.py:12-25), reference construction and assert_close check (infer.py:44-45), reference.pt/result.json writing, warmup and the 15 timed repeat samples with peak-memory queries (infer.py:49-65) are benchmark-harness infrastructure outside the repeated work.
